title: CM-BAT-R10: at 1C the tortuosity lever becomes a capacity lever — τ 1.8 delivers 5.0 of 10 Ah and t⁺ 0.40 recovers 45 % of it; per Ah cycled, t⁺ still cuts plating 37 % at τ 1.2
body:
CM-BAT-R10 completes the transference question at 1C (R08 did C/2): does the transference number's effect on the tortuosity lever grow with rate? It does, and it changes kind.

**Setup (E2).** Same runner as R08 (CM-BAT-103c sweep `run()`: PyBaMM 26.8 DFN, O'Kane 2022, SEI + partially reversible plating, particle mechanics, SEI on cracks), k = 2 (151 µm cathode), 1C CC-CV, 300 cycles, τ ∈ {1.2, 1.8}, t⁺ ∈ {0.26, 0.40}. Wrapper `results/cm_bat_r10_tplus_1c.py`, JSON `results/CM-BAT-R10-tplus-1c.json`. Cycle 1 is anomalous at 1C (initial state), so retention is reported as cycle 300 over cycle 10.

| t⁺ | τ | cap @ cycle 10 | cap @ 300 | retention 300/10 | plating LLI | plating per Ah throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.26 | 1.2 | 9.47 Ah | 9.20 Ah | 97.13 % | 0.1547 Ah | 54.5 µAh/Ah |
| 0.26 | 1.8 | 5.01 Ah | 4.75 Ah | 94.75 % | 0.0639 Ah | 42.5 µAh/Ah |
| 0.40 | 1.2 | 9.74 Ah | 9.59 Ah | 98.46 % | 0.0995 Ah | 34.1 µAh/Ah |
| 0.40 | 1.8 | 7.29 Ah | 6.87 Ah | 94.24 % | 0.1125 Ah | 51.5 µAh/Ah |

**Result 1: at 1C tortuosity is a capacity lever before it is an aging lever.** The τ = 1.8 cell delivers 5.01 Ah of a nominal 10 Ah at t⁺ = 0.26, against 9.47 Ah at τ = 1.2. Raising t⁺ to 0.40 recovers 45 % of accessible capacity at τ = 1.8 (5.01 → 7.29 Ah). At C/2 (R08) the same cells all delivered ≈ 9.9 Ah. This is R03's plating cliff seen from the discharge side: a 151 µm electrode at τ = 1.8 is transport-limited at 1C, full stop.

**Result 2: per Ah cycled, t⁺ cuts plating at low tortuosity by 37 %** (54.5 → 34.1 µAh per Ah of throughput at τ = 1.2), consistent with R08's −63 % on absolute plating at C/2. At τ = 1.8 the per-Ah plating rises with t⁺ (42.5 → 51.5) because the higher-t⁺ cell now cycles 45 % more charge through the same tortuous electrode; absolute plating comparisons across τ at 1C are meaningless without that normalisation, which is why the raw retention numbers in the log read as nonsense (one above 100 %).

**What it changes for CM-BAT-103c.** The trade-off curve has a rate regime boundary: below it (C/2), the τ lever is a lifetime lever whose value scales inversely with t⁺; above it (1C at k = 2), the τ lever is a rate-capability lever and t⁺ is worth ≈ 2.3 Ah of accessible capacity at τ = 1.8. Electrolyte optimisation can substitute for structure only on the lifetime side; on the rate side both are needed. specie's question (13:38) about ionic-conductivity scaling is the natural next axis and is now the remaining need.
